clue.text: Monks' open country airs!

parts.note: a plain is a stretch of flat open country
an air is a tune, so airs are songs

explanation.surface: An exclamation that monks sing songs about the open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, plainsong being the chant of monks, while 'open country' and 'airs' build it piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is the unaccompanied Gregorian chant sung in monasteries, so it is the music of monks.

clue.text: Not drinking when in real trouble following

indicators.note: the abstinence letters sit in the middle of the jumbled word, as the clue's in says
real in trouble is the word real put into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone stays sober only when they are in real trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns REAL into LAER, and 'in' puts TT inside it after LA.
explanation.definitionFit: The latter is the one named second, the one coming after in a list.

clue.text: Devise a fashionable outlet

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a vent is an opening that lets air or steam out

explanation.surface: Come up with a stylish shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlet' suggests a shop, but here it is an opening for air.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent something is to devise it, creating it for the first time.

clue.text: One who drinks at dinner?

explanation.surface: Someone who has a drink with an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sups, or drinks in sips, is a supper; supper is also the evening meal, a dinner.

clue.text: Children in handcuffs

explanation.surface: Children who have been handcuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers is British slang for small kids, and also an old slang word for handcuffs.

clue.text: Sprayed mace about but recovered consciousness

indicators.note: the word mace is scattered like a spray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: round can mean about, as in round the house

explanation.surface: Someone sprayed with mace briefly passed out but then woke again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprayed' turns MACE into CAME. Mace here is the irritant spray, which fits the picture of someone knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round is an idiom for waking up after fainting.

clue.text: Against citizenship for worker vic in chemical company

parts.note: a worker is a worker ant, the commonest crossword ant
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British chemical company
vic is taken as written

explanation.surface: A workman called Vic at a chemical firm opposes civic duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the worker and Vic before the company, but the answer puts the pieces in the order ANT, ICI, VIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticivic describes being opposed to civic duties or the rights and duties of a citizen.

clue.text: Making about a thousand for burning

indicators.note: making about a thousand means making goes round the thousand, so it is a container

parts.note: creating something is making it
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone producing about a thousand items to be burned.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremating a body means reducing it to ashes by fire.

clue.text: One who prohibits showing the flag?

explanation.surface: Someone who forbids displaying the flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is someone who bans things, and a banner is also a flag or standard.

clue.text: Lid over the cooker?

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat, and a tall hat shares its name with the flue that rises above a kitchen range

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lid sits on top of the kitchen range.
explanation.definitionFit: A stovepipe is a tall silk hat, a lid in slang, and also the pipe carrying smoke up from a stove.

clue.text: Me? I fall into mud backwards with spiritualist!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: I fall into means the letter I drops inside the other word
mud backwards means the word mud is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that they have fallen backwards into mud along with a psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns MUD into DUM, and 'fall into' puts I inside it to make DIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium is a spiritualist who claims to pass messages from the dead.

clue.text: The two of us, being cockney, went to journalist and rambled on

indicators.note: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: the two of us could be me and her
ED is short for editor, the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Two people in London went to see a reporter and talked at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cockney' drops the H from ME AND HER, giving ME AND 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly, like a winding river, so rambled is a close synonym.

clue.text: Thus the doctor's got one from Russian union

parts.note: so means thus, in that way

indicators.note: the doctor's got one means the doctor holds the one inside

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: So the doctor has received one from a Russian federation.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was an elected council in Russia, and the Soviet Union was the USSR.

clue.text: Dashing hurriedly off sinking ship

explanation.surface: Rats rushing off a ship that is going down.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuttling means running with quick short steps, and also sinking a vessel deliberately by holing it.

clue.text: Chap to transport, one with his own orchestra

parts.note: a chap is a man
taken as written
a van is a vehicle for transport
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man is asked to carry a musician who leads his own band.
explanation.definitionFit: Annunzio Mantovani was a popular Italian-born British conductor who led the Mantovani Orchestra.

clue.text: Get story wrong, so do not make connection

explanation.surface: Someone mixes up a tale and so fails to link things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate is both to narrate and to connect, so misrelating is telling inaccurately or linking wrongly.

clue.text: Enquire when king will appear

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Asking when the king will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to enquire, posing a question.

clue.text: A long time to mature

explanation.surface: It takes many years to grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a long era or a very long while, and to age is to grow older or ripen.

clue.text: Arabic pot

parts.note: pot here is the drug cannabis, and the word asked for comes from Arabic

explanation.definitionFit: Kif is a name for cannabis smoked in North Africa, from an Arabic word for pleasure.

clue.text: A layer of cloth

explanation.surface: A sheet of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A coating is a covering layer, and coating is also cloth for making coats.

clue.text: Poles at home first for gin cocktail — it advertises pub

indicators.note: at home first says the home piece goes before the poles

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mix, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: Polish people at home first order a gin cocktail, and it promotes a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests Polish people, but it is N and S. 'cocktail' turns GIN into IGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub sign hangs outside a British pub showing its name, so it advertises the tavern.

clue.text: Mail 1,000 francs into monetary fund

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
F is the abbreviation for francs

explanation.surface: Sending a thousand francs by post into a currency fund.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Monetary Fund was a planned European reserve fund, abbreviated by its initials.

clue.text: Animals shut mother up!

parts.note: mam is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for shut is read from the bottom

parts.note: to slam is to shut noisily

explanation.surface: Telling a mother to be quiet about creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' reads as be quiet, but 'up' turns SLAM into MALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammals are warm-blooded creatures that feed their young milk.

clue.text: Sign of disapproval, or strangeness of teachers?

parts.note: tut is a click of the tongue showing disapproval
taken as written
S is the physics symbol for strangeness, a property of quarks

explanation.surface: Asking whether teachers are marked by disapproval or oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutors are private teachers who coach students individually.

clue.text: Omit to obtain the French silk

parts.note: to fail to do something is to omit doing it
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Neglect to buy the French silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Faille is a soft ribbed fabric of silk or rayon.

clue.text: Miss computer technology — never mind!

parts.note: to skip something is to miss it out
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Telling someone to drop computing, it does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Skip it is an idiom telling someone to forget it, it does not matter.

clue.text: Some crank — Arab — has a place in turkey

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An eccentric Arab has a spot in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'has' into the definition; it is a link word, since the answer is a place, not something that has one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: Boarding every other term — quite mad!

indicators.note: every other term means taking alternate letters of the word term

parts.note: barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Boarding school every other term would drive anyone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every other' takes E and M from TERM. BARKING is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarking means going aboard a ship or plane.

clue.text: Speaks honestly of aims

explanation.surface: Talks frankly about goals.
explanation.definitionFit: To level with someone is to be frank, and to level a gun is to aim it.

clue.text: Drop work, then ian can catch tube

parts.note: to fall is to drop
op is short for opus, a musical work
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stop working, and then Ian can get on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' suggests the London Underground, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fallopian tube is the duct carrying eggs from ovary to womb, so the adjective stands for that tube.

clue.text: The number a number try — not right!

parts.note: nine is a number

indicators.note: R is the abbreviation for right, removed from the word try

explanation.surface: A muddled sentence about numbers and an attempt that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from TRY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, nine times ten.

clue.text: Tails seen, perhaps, as necessary

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of tails seen might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Seeing tails is perhaps a must.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TAILS SEEN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, absolutely required.
